title: Escaping Model Collapse via Synthetic Data Verification: Near-term Improvements and Long-term Convergence
claim: Retraining on self-generated data degrades quality, but filtering it with an external verifier preserves and improves quality, approaching the real-data upper bound.
layout: 4 columns, left-to-right, branching green/red arrows into two sample grids
description: A left-to-right flow of MNIST digit grids, each 10 rows by 8 columns. On the far left is a grid of original real digits labeled "Original Data". An arrow labeled "VAE Trained on 500 Real Images" leads to a grid of blurry, noisy digits labeled "Initial Model". From there the flow splits into two diagonal arrows. The upper arrow has green italic text, "With Data Verification", and leads to a grid of clean, clear digits. The lower arrow has red text, "Without Data Verification", and leads to a grid of degraded, noisy, near-unrecognizable blobs. A shared caption between the two branches reads "Re-Trained on Synthetic Images after 40 Rounds". A dashed vertical line separates these from a final grid, "Directly Trained on All 60K Real Images", which shows sharp digits as the upper bound. The eye goes first to the contrast between the clean green-branch grid and the garbled red-branch grid.
caption: Iterative VAE Retraining on MNIST. Left: Original MNIST images (real data). Middle: Samples from a VAE trained on 500 real images. Right: Samples after 40 rounds of synthetic retraining. The top branch (green) uses verifier-filtered synthetic data, producing clearer and more realistic digits; the bottom branch (red) retrains without verification, leading to severe degradation and mode collapse. The final column shows a VAE trained on all 60K real images (upper bound on quality).
abstract: Synthetic data has been increasingly used to train frontier generative models. However, recent studies raise key concerns that iteratively retraining a generative model on its self-generated synthetic data may keep deteriorating model performance, a phenomenon often coined model collapse. In this paper, we investigate ways to modify the synthetic retraining process to avoid model collapse, and even possibly help reverse the trend from collapse to improvement. Our key finding is that by injecting information through an external synthetic data verifier, whether a human or a better model, synthetic retraining will not cause model collapse. Specifically, we situate our theoretical analysis in the fundamental linear regression setting, showing that verifier-guided retraining can yield near-term improvements, but ultimately drives the parameter estimate to the verifier's "knowledge center" in the long run. Our theory further predicts that, unless the verifier is perfectly reliable, these early gains will plateau and may even reverse. Indeed, our experiments across linear regression, Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) trained on MNIST, and fining-tuning SmolLM2-135M on the XSUM task confirm these theoretical insights.
